os-5-11.alt: A block of skin cut through one hair. The hair rises from a teardrop-shaped pocket that dips down through the dermis to the fat below. At its base, a swollen bulb wraps around a small knot of blood vessels, and a layer of dividing cells sits just above that knot. Colored sheaths line the pocket around the hair. A lobed gland opens into the pocket partway up, and a slanting strip of muscle runs from the pocket's side up toward the surface. A boxed inset marks the part of the hair above the skin, which has an inner core, a middle layer and an outer coat.

os-5-13.alt: Two drawings of a fingertip. On the left, the top of the finger shows the nail plate, its white free edge at the tip, a pale crescent near its base, a thin band of skin lying over the base of the plate, and the folds of skin along its base and sides. On the right, a side view cut lengthwise shows the nail plate lying on the skin, its hidden base tucked under a fold of skin, the thickened skin under the tip, and the layers of skin and the bone inside the finger.

os-5-14.alt: A block of skin showing a sweat gland: a tight coil of tubing deep in the dermis, with a single duct that winds up through the dermis and epidermis and opens at a tiny pore on the surface. Several pores dot the skin surface, and hairs, fat lobules, blood vessels and nerve fibers fill the rest of the block.
